title: Family praises jury's recommendations
article: The family of a man who died in police custody in Fort St. John is praising the jury's recommendations at a coroner's inquest and hope various agencies follow them to prevent similar deaths.
The five-member jury ruled Larry McPherson's August 2007 death was an accidental cocaine-induced sudden death.
McPherson, 31, died after a struggle with several Mounties.
The inquest heard McPherson was high on drugs for several days before his death and that five officers had a hard time restraining him.

The jury called on the RCMP, B.C. Ambulance Service and the Office of the Fire Commissioner to ensure all relevant information is communicated to responding emergency service providers before they arrive on a scene.

The jury also recommended personnel be trained in recognizing and responding to people in a state of excited delirium, a state of mind characterized by confusion, super-human strength and bizarre behaviour.
Jurors also called for increased funding and resources to raise awareness and provide support to children with learning disabilities, something McPherson could have benefited from.
"(The jury) couldn't have done much better than that," said Alberta McPherson, Larry's mother.
